A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: V4 reports original synthetic and real-measurement reconstruction experiments, baseline comparisons, noise and training-data ablations, and 3D reconstruction results.

after.justification: V6 retains those empirical results and adds Two-Step baseline results, auxiliary-loss experiments, and a reconstruction failure example.

M1.justification: The proposed method retains the same coordinate-conditioned MLP, Fourier positional encoding, scattered-field inputs, MSE training objective, and feed-forward inference. TV and perceptual losses appear only as additional ablation variants; they do not replace the proposed MSE-only method.

E1.justification: Both versions use Circular, MNIST, Institut Fresnel, 3D MNIST, and 3D ShapeNet, retaining the same reconstruction tasks and noise/transmitter coverage. The added analyses use existing coverage. The IF comparison moves from the appendix into the main text.

E2.justification: V6 adds Two-Step, attributed to Yao et al. (2019), to both transmitter configurations in Table 1 for Circular and MNIST at both noise levels. It has no IF results. The seven existing baseline methods remain.

E3.justification: New Appendix D.3 introduces controlled comparisons of MSE-only training against MSE plus TV or perceptual loss on single-transmitter MNIST at 5% and 30% noise. Existing splits, metrics, and training budgets remain unchanged. Noise-specific model training is newly disclosed, without establishing a change to existing experiments.

E4.justification: V6 adds a loss-choice ablation in Appendix D.3 and Table 5, testing whether auxiliary smoothness or perceptual supervision helps. Figure 9 adds a thin-structure failure example. Existing noise robustness, training-data-size analyses, and supplementary reconstructions are retained.

E5.justification: Both Appendix D.1 sections report three independent trials with independently sampled, scaled Gaussian noise. Table 4 retains the same means and standard deviations. V6 adds no new uncertainty-reporting procedure or increased run count.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results in Tables 1–4 and the 3D results remain unchanged. Table 1 adds Two-Step scores; Table 5 adds loss-variant results, including single-transmitter MNIST at 5% noise PSNRs of 26.00 with TV and 26.20 with perceptual loss versus 26.09 for MSE alone. Figure 9 adds a qualitative failure result.

T1.justification: The scattering equations, discretization, inverse-mapping formulation, and relative-error definition remain mathematically unchanged. V6 introduces no new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or derivation; its parenthesis correction is typographical.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: end-to-end data-driven inversion, distribution priors compensating for sparse measurements, and accurate single-transmitter reconstruction. Additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: V6 clarifies that distribution priors are learned implicitly rather than supplied through explicit generative modules. It newly acknowledges thin-structure failures and their deployment implications, while retaining the fixed-sensor-layout limitation. Appendix D.3 interprets mixed auxiliary-loss effects as support for MSE-only training.

D1.justification: V6 discloses official baseline-code use, separate models for each noise level, the single-transmitter location (3, 0), and the three-coordinate input for the existing 3D extension. It explicitly states that code and models are released at an updated project address. Appendix C.3's architecture, optimizer, hardware, and training details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V6 adds references on diffusion and plug-and-play priors, additional electromagnetic inversion approaches including Two-Step, and auxiliary losses. It distinguishes its implicit data prior from explicit generative priors. The existing related-work organization and principal positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: Most prose and the section sequence are retained. V6 makes local clarifications and corrections, including Rytov terminology, updates affiliations and correspondence information, adds acknowledgments, and introduces Appendix D.3. The extensive visual reformatting does not constitute extensive narrative rewriting.

P2.justification: V6 comprehensively changes the single-column layout to two columns and enlarges and repositions displays. Figure 1 moves onto the first page, the appendix IF comparison becomes main-text Figure 6, Figures 4–5 are condensed, the ShapeNet figure gains a failure panel, and Table 5 is added.

improvement.justification: The added comparator and loss ablation modestly strengthen validation, while the explicit failure case and clearer experimental disclosures improve transparency. The gains are limited: core results remain unchanged, and the new perceptual-loss ablation omits implementation details and cites a machine-translation paper as reference [20].
